text:
Ari P: Quick check on the Alerting > SLO editor: I added a 'Channel-specific preview' button that expands an inline rail showing a sample notification per selected channel. Mock: https://figma.redwood/channel-previews (WIP)
Nina (PM): This is great for copy parity. Two asks: 1) make it obvious which channels strip markdown, 2) keyboard-only users must be able to open each channel preview.
Jonas - Eng: Implementation note: we'll fetch channel render rules from /api/channels/:id/rules and client-side render. Example response is an array, but we won't paste the JSON here.
Priya: UX nit: the preview header currently reads 'Channel preview (sim)'. Can we shorten? My suggestion: 'Preview (no send)'.
Ari P: Good. Alternative: 'Preview only  no messages sent'. Which fits better in the tight header?
Priya: 'Preview only' is fine, add a tooltip with 'No outbound messages will be sent during preview.'
AccessibilityBot: Checklist: - ensure each channel preview has role="dialog" when expanded, - focus moves to close button on open, - Esc closes and returns focus to channel row, - add aria-describedby linking to the 'no messages' helper.
Nina (PM): Visual: when a channel strips markdown (e.g., SMS), show a small badge 'Plain text' and a collapsed 'Formatting differences' disclosure.
Jonas - Eng: Perf note: avoid rendering full message bodies for long channel lists; render titles and load body on expand.
Priya: Mobile: inline rail becomes full-screen sheet. Ensure the sheet title shows channel name + badge.
Ari P: I'll update mocks to use the shorter header, add the plain-text badge, and include keyboard flows. Also I'll add a tiny contrast tweak on the disclosure chevron.
Nina (PM): One more copy micro: for the disclosure use 'Formatting notes' rather than 'Formatting differences'  shorter and clearer.
Priya: For tiny pill label when space is tight use 'Plain' instead of 'Plain text'.
AccessibilityBot: Added items: [ ] role/dialog on expand, [ ] focus trap + return, [ ] aria-describedby helper, [ ] mobile sheet title, [ ] lazy-load bodies.
Ari P: Thanks all. If anyone wants to propose even shorter pill/copy options for very small screens, drop them here and I'll try them in the prototype.
